basis: Lipodystrophy, diabetes, skin papules and cardiomyopathy define the syndrome; hepatic steatosis is also a defining manifestation.
Myoclonus and dystonia define a neurologic movement disorder.
Structural enlargement of the tongue; the mouth belongs to the gastrointestinal axis.
Isolated familial dilated cardiomyopathy; no neurologic involvement inferred from PSEN1.
Inherited triglyceride metabolism disorder; pancreatitis is a separate diagnosis. Xanthomas and lipemia retinalis do not establish functional organ damage.
Focal epilepsy syndrome defined by recurrent focal seizures.
Myeloid malignancy involving bone marrow and circulating blood cells.
Occlusion of the vertebral artery; cerebral infarction is a separate complication and is not inherent.
Umbrella for atypical reproductive and genital development; endocrine dysfunction is not established across the group.
Combined lipase deficiency disrupts lipid metabolism; subcutaneous fat loss reported in 1/1 patient supports skin involvement. Pancreatitis is a separate diagnosis.
Spinal motor pathway disease with peripheral neuropathy; urinary symptoms and weakness reflect neurologic dysfunction. Skeletal abnormalities occur in under 30%.
Adenocarcinoma originates in the glandular epithelium of the appendix.
The supplied syndrome synonym identifies cerebellar atrophy, intellectual disability, juvenile cataracts and myopathy as defining features.
Defined by colorectal polyposis and colorectal cancer; no additional organ damage established.
Embryonal malignancy arising in the central nervous system.
Superficial corneal dystrophy confined to the eye.
Defined by disorders of the liver, bile ducts or gallbladder, all within the hepatic axis.
Chest wall malignancy involves the musculoskeletal wall of the thorax; pulmonary origin and lymphoma mechanism do not apply across this umbrella.
Presynaptic neuromuscular junction disorder; ophthalmoplegia and respiratory weakness reflect neural transmission failure. Contracture and ileus are secondary manifestations.
Intestinal polyposis and multiple bony exostoses are the defining manifestations.
Polyp originates in the ureter, which belongs to the renal axis.
Limb skeletal dysplasia with shortened or fused bones and dislocations; definition explicitly states normal intelligence, conflicting with the cognitive HPO annotation.
Congenital structural defect of the oral palate; middle-ear disease is a separately diagnosed complication.
BK polyomavirus directly infects and damages renal tissue; the supplied hantavirus parent is inconsistent with the named infection.
Inborn error of valine metabolism; cardiomyopathy and developmental impairment are occasional, below 30%, and most screened patients lack such damage.
